source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Once roots are visible filling the wrapped medium (after roughly 2-3 months), the rooted branch is cut away just below the new root ball and moved into a nursery pot filled with a light growing mix to hold and harden off before field planting.

During this hardening stage the young plant should be kept in partial shade and watered regularly but not waterlogged; scorching in direct sun or drying out at this stage can kill an otherwise successful marcot. After the plant has produced new leaves and looks vigorous - typically after several more weeks - it is ready to transplant into the orchard.
